title: The American Civil War
subject: histoire
description: From **1861** to **1865**, the United States tore itself apart: more than **620,000** dead. At the heart of the war, slavery, national unity, and the birth of a stronger federal state.

hero.hook: The deadliest war in American history, fought for the Union and against slavery.

blocks.text: From **1861** to **1865**, the United States lived through its gravest crisis: the Civil War. The North (the Union) against the South (the Confederacy). More than **620,000** dead.
The war turned a young republic into an industrial power, at the cost of a lasting wound to national unity and a reckoning with slavery.
The **North** was industrializing, built on wages and protective tariffs. The **South** stayed rural, rich on cotton grown by **4 million** enslaved people.

blocks.caption: A Southern plantation: slavery at the heart of the Confederate economy

blocks.text: The argument also ran over **[[States' rights vs. the federal government]]**: who decides on slavery, the individual state or Washington? The election of **Abraham Lincoln** (**November 1860**), a Republican opposed to any spread of slavery, who won without a single Southern vote, set secession off. Seven states founded the Confederacy, with **[[Jefferson Davis]]** as president, and wrote slavery into their constitution.
Before the war, people usually said “the United States *are*,” in the plural. Afterward the singular took over, “the United States *is*”: one indivisible nation.

On **April 12, 1861**, Southern guns opened fire on Fort Sumter in South Carolina. The short war everyone expected turned industrial. At **Antietam** (**September 17, 1862**), **23,000** men were killed or wounded in twelve hours, the bloodiest day in American military history.

The failure of **[[Robert E. Lee]]**, the leading Confederate general, let Lincoln sign the **[[Emancipation Proclamation]]** (**January 1, 1863**), which freed the enslaved people of the rebel states. The war for the Union became a war for freedom as well, which closed the door on European support for the South. **Gettysburg** (July **1863**) broke the Confederate advance.

blocks.caption: A Civil War battle: industrial violence on a scale never seen before

blocks.text: **[[Ulysses Grant]]**, general in chief of the Union armies, fought a war of attrition. His lieutenant **William Tecumseh Sherman** laid Georgia waste on his “March to the Sea.” Lee surrendered at **Appomattox** on **April 9, 1865**.

blocks.caption: Abraham Lincoln, president of the Union, killed five days after Appomattox

blocks.text: Five days later, Lincoln was assassinated by **John Wilkes Booth**, a Southern actor. **[[Reconstruction]]**, the rebuilding of the South, began without him. In December **1865**, the [[13th Amendment]] abolished slavery across the whole country.
The war also pushed surgery forward: doctors such as **Gurdon Buck** performed the first facial reconstructions on soldiers disfigured by Minié balls.

Under **[[Reconstruction]]** (**1865-1877**), African Americans voted and won office. Then came the backlash: the **[[Ku Klux Klan]]** (**1865**), a white terrorist organization, the withdrawal of federal troops (**1877**), and the Jim Crow segregation laws. Legal segregation would last almost a century.
On the map, a united nation with no legal slavery. On the ground, a deep racial divide. And the tools of a future world power: heavy industry, railroads, a strong federal state.

blocks.text: The Civil War (**1861-1865**) held the United States together and abolished slavery, at a cost of **620,000** dead, while leaving a racial divide that the Jim Crow laws would carry on.
